newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall Street vigour aids European markets.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall Street vigour aids European markets.

text.p: Wall Street's return to the record books overnight breathed new vigour into some of Europe's stock markets on Thursday, but the dollar steadied off its highs.
Bond markets were mixed in early trade, with German traders predicting that worries over a power struggle in Russia could undermine government bonds.

And crude oil prices hovered well below this week's six-year highs of more than $25 a barrel, with benchmark Brent December quoted at $23.92. U.S. blue-chip stocks shook off early selling pressure on Wednesday and set record highs for the second time in three days as investors sought the safety of big companies more likely to deliver solid earnings.

The Dow Jones industrial average's 16-point rise helped London and Frankfurt make a firm start after their record-breaking pace faltered on Wednesday. But French shares succumbed to further consolidation and Frankfurt later fell back.
Although some U.S. analysts said they detected a flight to quality stocks amid concerns about Wall Street's ability to sustain its rally, buyers were still out looking for bargains.
Investor attention is likely to focus later on U.S. industrial production and capacity utilisation numbers for September, due at 1315 GMT.
The Wall Street bounce reassured British investors, boosting the blue chip FTSE 00 index in early trade along with a rise by drug company Zeneca on renewed bid speculation.
The FTSE 100 was up 13.7 at 4,038.1 by 0930 GMT, with some strategists predicting the London bull run was set to continue, despite Wednesday's retreat on inflation worries.
"A brief period of weakness soon could be construed as the last chance to get in and buy at reasonable levels," Robin Griffiths, technical analyst at HSBC James Capel, said in a research note.
However, continuing concern about a possible hike in British interest rates after a string of economic figures could keep immediate business mixed, traders said.
French shares opened easier in further consolidation after hitting a high for the year on Tuesday.
Shares in French conglomerate Lagardere Groupe requoted at 170 francs a share on Thursday after being suspended limit up at several successive attempts to trade during the morning.
The shares closed on Tuesday at 133.10 francs and were suspended on Wednesday as the French government announced Lagardere was its preferred bidder in the privatisation of Thomson SA.
German shares were well-supported at the start of trade but later fell back to just below opening levels.
By 0930 GMT the 30 share DAX index was trading around its opening levels with dealers saying there was a lack of follow-through buying.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar steadied just under 1.54 marks in Europe after retreating from Wednesday's peak.

A stream of comments from German Bundesbank officials this week has cooled expectations that Italy and Spain will make the first phase of European monetary union, prompting the mark to firm against the peseta and lira.
Traders said sterling was also being sold for yen as the pound succumbed to profit-taking following its steep climb.
"Most of what we're seeing on the bond and currency markets at the moment is just profit-taking, with no specific news trigger," said Wilkes at Julius Baer.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5365 marks and 112.09 yen, compared with 1.5383 and 112.22 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
London - The FTSE index was up 13.7 points at 4,038.1.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was trading up 0.11 points at 2,715.01.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 0.16 points at 2,158.36.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $380.75 an ounce, down from $381.75 at the London close on Wednesday. Silver started at $4.99 against $5.06.
